requirements.requirement: node2 exposes an HTTP service on TCP 8080 reachable over the private network shared with node1/node3
requirements.summary: No listener existed on port 8080 initially (cmd-fb3d5b645f204f17 showed only sshd listening). Executor created and enabled a systemd-managed python http.server bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 (cmd-01d473347fb1404b), opened the firewalld port (cmd-4009a508367048ec), and node3 confirmed reachability via curl returning 200 over the private IP (cmd-7ab3e82583b84fe1). Post-restart the service remained active and reachable (cmd-70179e5dd4704567, cmd-9e0d394acfe147f6).

requirements.requirement: node1 authoritatively answers DNS for app.internal on the shared private network, allowing node3 to reach the service by name without any local hosts-file entry
requirements.summary: node1's dnsmasq was already listening on the shared LAN address 10.100.229.10:53 (cmd-2f12c7cfd63b4411). Executor added a UCI dhcp domain record mapping app.internal -> 10.100.229.11, committed, and restarted dnsmasq (cmd-d8a00a36b613472c), verified locally via nslookup (cmd-5f094829cc9548c1). node3's resolver was pointed at node1 (cmd-8658991d23e041e2), and node3 was confirmed to resolve app.internal via DNS, reach the HTTP service (cmd-653b6fb374424cf0), and to have no matching /etc/hosts entry (cmd-cd11abc72c4f47c4). Post-restart of all three nodes, DNS resolution and HTTP reachability from node3 with no hosts entry were re-verified (cmd-b215d69d56794544, cmd-9e0d394acfe147f6, cmd-f9009e7fc60a44cc).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated on all three managed nodes (node1, node2, node3)
requirements.summary: For each node the executor captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state baseline, issued and acknowledged a reboot, observed connection timeouts during the transition, confirmed a new distinct boot_id afterward, and re-verified recovered service/data/cluster state (dnsmasq+UCI record+DNS resolution on node1; app-http.service+8080 listener on node2; resolv.conf persistence+no hosts entry+DNS/HTTP reachability on node3). Boot-id transitions match the fixed lifecycle snapshots exactly (node1 e416c8db→03f90979, node2 dfdea52d→d9045a76, node3 f43afa1c→abe89000), independently cross-confirming the restart evidence.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node2 now runs a firewalled HTTP service on 8080 reachable from node3, and node1's dnsmasq authoritatively resolves app.internal to node2's private IP for node3 (which was repointed to use node1 as resolver) with no local hosts-file entry. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated across all three nodes, with boot-identity transitions cross-verified against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. A single failed reboot attempt on node1 due to a missing 'nohup' binary was a harmless, state-free troubleshooting step that was immediately corrected.
limitations: Restart-protocol evidence and functional DNS/HTTP checks rely on executor-run commands rather than an independent verifier probe, though boot-id values are cross-checked against the fixed collector snapshots for node1/node2/node3.
No direct evidence was captured of other network clients (e.g., node2 itself) resolving app.internal via node1, since only node3's resolution was required and tested by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to task outcomes or the restart protocol: creating the systemd HTTP service and firewall rule on node2, the UCI dnsmasq domain record on node1, and node3's NetworkManager DNS repoint were each necessary and were retained as intended final state. One initial reboot attempt on node1 (cmd-b458d4bc3de14d2b, using 'nohup' which was not present on the BusyBox image) failed silently and caused no actual state change, as confirmed by the unchanged boot_id in the immediate follow-up check (cmd-44cc087afb9240d6) and the diagnostic that revealed 'nohup: not found' (cmd-37f0da5b99aa4f62); it was promptly corrected with a working reboot invocation (cmd-b0600d5bb4af4a08) and left no residue. No unrestored, broad, or destructive mutations were observed; the after-executor lifecycle diff shows only expected additions (8080 listener, reboot logs, per-boot systemd-private tmp dirs) with no failed services or package-health regressions on any node.
